content: {"summary":"During the early‑morning window on 23 July 2026 both notification‑worker pods logged DNS lookups that sometimes took several seconds and produced EAI_AGAIN errors. The evidence points to the cluster’s default ndots:5 causing short names to be expanded into many queries, increasing the chance of lost replies that are retried, which adds ~10 s latency.","likely_cause":"Cluster default ndots:5 expands short names into many DNS queries, leading to occasional lost replies and retries that cause 5‑10 s lookup delays and EAI_AGAIN errors.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Both notification-worker pods experienced slow DNS lookups and occasional EAI_AGAIN errors.","evidence_ids":["INC-0179#0"],"quote":"Both workers resolved names slowly, and a few lookups finished in `EAI_AGAIN`"},{"text":"The slowdown was caused by the cluster default ndots:5 expanding short names into many DNS queries.","evidence_ids":["INC-0179#0"],"quote":"With the cluster default of `ndots:5` in place, a short name is expanded"},{"text":"Lost DNS replies and retries added about 10 seconds latency to some lookups.","evidence_ids":["RB-021#5"],"quote":"Two lost replies on two different queries of the same lookup, each recovered by its retry, cost about 10 s"}],"next_checks":["Check the dnsConfig of the notification‑worker Deployment for an ndots override","Inspect CoreDNS logs for query loss or timeouts during the incident window","Measure libuv thread‑pool usage and consider increasing UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE","Run a controlled DNS lookup benchmark with ndots:5 vs a lower value"]}
